About This Tool

Onelife Fitness Competitive Map visualizes the competitive landscape around each of our 63 club locations. It answers the question: which locations face the most competitive pressure, and from whom?

Data Sources

Competitor locations come from Google Places API (Nearby Search + chain-specific Text Search for 18 major gym brands). Drive times are from OSRM (Open Source Routing Machine) using OpenStreetMap road data—no live traffic, but road type speeds are modeled (highways faster than local roads). Coordinates were validated via Google Geocoding API. Data as of February 2026.

Controls

Club selector: Pick any Onelife location to see its competitive environment.

Top N competitors: How many competitors to display on the map (sorted by nearest drive time).

Advanced Filters (expandable):

  • Brand Similarity (1–10): How closely a competitor resembles Onelife’s offering. 10 = near-identical (LA Fitness, Gold’s, Crunch), 1 = not really a competitor (hotel gym, dance studio).
  • Competitor Dues: Estimated monthly membership price. Filters by price tier.
  • Max drive time/distance: Only include competitors within this range.
  • Distance metric: What “distance” means in the formula—drive time (minutes), drive distance (road miles), or straight-line (as the crow flies).
  • Decay (α): Controls how fast competitive pressure drops off with distance. Higher α means nearby competitors dominate; lower α spreads influence more evenly. Default is 1.5.

Outputs

Rank (#N of 63): This location’s competitive intensity rank across the portfolio. #1 = most competitive pressure. Color goes from red (#1) to blue (#63).

Intensity (X/100): Normalized competitive intensity score. 100 = the most intense location with all filters off.

The “?” button: Shows the full breakdown—formula, top contributors, and an interpretation of this location’s competitive position.

Clubs Ranked: All 63 locations ranked by competitive intensity. Click any row to jump to that location. “Copy” exports tab-delimited data for Excel.

Map markers: Dot size = brand similarity. Line thickness = proximity. Hover for full competitor details (name, chain, drive time, dues estimate, rating).

Methodology

Competitive intensity uses a gravity model:

Intensity = Σ (similarity_score / (1 + distance)α)

This sums each competitor’s contribution, weighted by how similar they are and penalized by how far away they are. A score-10 gym 2 minutes away is a much bigger competitive threat than a score-3 yoga studio 25 minutes away.

Coverage

63 Onelife locations • 6,018 competitor pairs • ~2,000 unique competitor names

95% of competitors scored for brand similarity • 87% with dues estimates • 100% with drive times

18 major chains searched individually to fill gaps in generic search results.

Built by Braff & Co. using Google Places API, OSRM, Leaflet, and OpenStreetMap.
